notes.title: Arttista Version 2.0.4 Update & Game Character Creation Tutorial
notes.content:
We’re excited to announce that [b]Arttista has received a major update to Version 2.0.4[/b]! This new version brings a powerful new feature: [b]Object Scaling[/b]! You can now scale objects horizontally, vertically, or both, [b]without affecting the object’s outline[/b]. This gives you more control and flexibility in your designs.

Along with this update, we’ve also released a new tutorial series on our Arttista YouTube channel, dedicated to [b]Game Character Creation[/b]. The series consists of 3 comprehensive tutorials:

[list]
[*]1/3: Drawing a Game Character – Learn how to create and design this character.
[previewyoutube=cRZbqOJhavE;full][/previewyoutube]

[*]2/3: Animating Your Character – Bring this character to life with animation techniques.
[previewyoutube=gVAe-A1hgCA;full][/previewyoutube]

[*]3/3: Exporting to Sprite Sheet – Discover how to export your animated character into a sprite sheet for game development.
[previewyoutube=_jqdbR3OW8k;full][/previewyoutube]
[/list]
Check out the full series on our YouTube channel, and take your game character creation skills to the next level with Arttista!

notes.title: Arttista 2.0 is here and ready for you!
notes.content:
After 3 years of satisfying Steam users with a lot of improvements and updates,[b] Arttista arrives in version 2.0[/b]. It brings so waited features like [b]video exporting and animation soft interpolation[/b],
besides a lot of other new features and bug fixes that were made.

Arttista has grow and it's more mature than never.

A lot more will come in feature versions.

Soon as you run Arttista 2.0 for the first time, Arttista will show you every new little thing and what changed.

[b]One of the coolest new things are Tracks[/b]. Now you can add tracks and assign keyframes and objects to them, what gives you much more control and production capacible.

The video export, for now, export videos to [b]AVI file format using RAW or MJpeg codec[/b]. Of course, this codecs are not great when we speak about final file size. It's because they are made to be quality lossless codec, where you can export your animations to a full quality video to be used in any video editor without lose production quality.

But soon, others codecs and video formats will come.

Stay tuned and thanks to be part of Arttista during all these 3 years.

What is new:

[list]
[*] Animation video export
[*] Animation soft interpolation
[*] Tracks
[*] Interpolation button on timeline
[*] Now you can create and delete keyframes on timeline using mouse double click
[*] Bug fixes
[/list]

notes.title: What? Arttista 1.9.12 Is here with "Inverse Kinematics". You need check it out!
notes.content:
We are pretty excited that [b]Arttista 1.9.12 brings Inverse Kinematics[/b]. With IK, you can control bones hierarchically just controlling a single bone almost like in real life, giving much more natural aspect to animation, besides turning the whole animation process more easy to complete. Now, if you mix this new feature with Arttista "Pose Merging", you can have your 2D character in a lot of angle views, obeying the same single skeleton, almost like it happens in a 3D character. 

Just check it out for your self. Watch the video. 

[previewyoutube=mvmcxv_RFNg;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]1.9.12 Changelog:[/b]

[list]
[*] New: Inverse Kinematics
[*] New: Bones Filter when press "Q"
[*] New: Deselect points when keep "shift" down while using circular selection mode
[*] New: New ways of select objects at front and behind
[*] And a lot of bug fixes
[/list]

notes.title: Oh My Gosh Honey! Arttista 1.9 is Available Now!
notes.content:
The moment has come. [b]Arttista has finally a SVG file importer.[/b] It's so cool to say it, cause a lot of people have been requested this feature and it's finally done. The SVG importer is still experimental, but it should works everytime. Due to Arttista mix vector and raster technics, some SVG files miss some properties after imported. The idea is to making SVG File Importer better each version.

Beside this, [b]Arttista now brings it's Color Palette Widget, where you can save and modify your own palettes without go to that Color Dialog every time. [/b]

Now, [b]it's also possible to enter each slider value directly typing the value.[/b]

Just check it out when your Arttista 1.9 opens for first time, a new window will show you all the changes in this version and how to use them.

There was also, a lot of bug fixes.

So.. thats it. 

Hope you like it.

Arttista 1.9 Changelog:
[list]
[*] New: Experimental support for SVG vectors files importing
[*] New: Added Color Palette Widget	
[*] New: Now you can easily swap foreground and background color
[*] New: Now you can edit every slider typing it's values
[*] New: New visual elements that explain every slider
[*] Fixes: Bug fixes
[/list]

notes.title: Arttista 1.8.4 is in da' house
notes.content:
Hello there! We are proud to announce Arttista 1.8.4 and also a new [b]2D Animated Short Film Made in Arttista, called "Wild"[/b].  From time to time, we create short animation movies to test Arttista features. This way, we can feel what else could be missing on it and start to create new features in Arttista besides to find and fix bugs.  Wild was enterily created inside Arttista and no other software was used for illustration, coloring, shading and animation. All the drawings created during the process will be available as "Examples" shiped with Arttista next verstion(1.8.5). The ideia behind Wild was to show that is possible create complex animations with complex shading and forms, resulting in a awesome 3D aspect. Don't forget to check it out what is new is 1.8.4 version after watch Wild.

[b]So check it out [/b]"Wild"[previewyoutube=gYmxNeqTZzU;full][/previewyoutube]

Check it out [b]Arttista 1.8.4 changelog:[/b]

[list]
[*]   New: Now there is a new button on Animation Panel, that when enabled, will force animation to be synched with your drawing frame per seconds, droping frames if necessary when rendering is slow.

[*]     New: Now there is a new bone mode in the object editor panel, that when enabled, will highglight all points that are related to a bone when mouse cursor is over this same bone. This way, all the skin of a bone will be hightlighted for conference purpose.

[*]     New: Now you can use alt+scroll(mouse) to change size of circular selection mode area.

[*]     Bugfix: Memory dealloc bug fix in Windows and MacOS versions.

[*]     Bugfix: Removed unecessary files int Linux version.

[*]     Bugfix: A huge, huge, very huge amount of bug fixes in interpolation, rendering and user interface.
[/list]

notes.title: Arttista 1.8.3 Are Finally Ready for Download
notes.content:
Hello folks. April is Arttista birthday on Steam. 2 years has passed from first day around here, and since then we have released version after version and received a lot of good feedback and excelent features requests.  This is what is different on Steam: The Community that is part of it. It is not a simple relationship between a software vendor and their clients. This made Arttista growing up so fast. We just want to thank you all and say that Arttista 1.8.3 is ready to rock.

Thus, you can watch this video where we talk about whats new in this version
[previewyoutube=L7VcvcWl7RQ;full][/previewyoutube]


[h2][b]Changelog:[/b][/h2]

[list]
[*] Now is possible to hide old objects when new objects are merged to your draw even if they dont belong to some bone. Before this version, only objects that belong to a bone could be automatically hided when new objects that belong do same bone are merged to current drawing.

[*] Now when Arttista is merging new content to an existing drawing, Arttista will hide old content on your drawing only if new content bones contains objects even if you has marked "hide" option before merge. What is does it mean? It means that, you can have in your shape library, only part of your characters like a hand for example, assigined to a skeleton. Then, when you will merge
this hand and it's skeleton into your current drawing where this character is on screen, only the current character hands will be hided giving place to the new hand imported. And this will
happen cause the rest of skeleton has no objects. Only the bone assigined to the new hand has object, that is the new hand of course. This way, for example, lets you have a lot of separeted parts of same character, in different angles or poses, inside shape library. Then you could use as the situation demands.

[*] Now when you do bones interpolation between poses inside keyframes, every bone that belong to other bone will obey hierarchically the parent bone. Before this version, you'd have to
select every related bone to do an interpolation. Now, for example, if you select only the 3th bone from a skeleton and do an interpolation, every bone after the 3th bone of this skeleton will be interpoladted too. This means the 4th, 5th, 6th, etc... Also, if you have another skeleton that belongs to this 3th bone, it will be entirely interpolated too.

[*] Bones interpolation bug fixes.

[/list]

You may watch this video to learn how and when to use it:

[previewyoutube=wyPvCE9YQBM;full][/previewyoutube]

[list]

[*] New: There is a new bone working mode called "Live Transformation" that applies live rotation to all points(skin) that belongs to a joint(bone) between keyframes while you're moving the mouse
[*] BugFix: On interpolation of objects that are hidden in some frames where interpolation will happen
[*] New: Now, when you select one or more objects, timeline shows where these objects are shown and where they are hidden
[*] BugFix: On in Ctrl+Z, that sometimes had lose some changes

Besides that, we are starting the Arttista Animation Guide. The Part one is ready to watch at

notes.title: Arttista 1.8.1 is finally on!
notes.content:
Arttista 1.8.1 was late, but is finally here. It brings new useful features and bug fixes. I also did a video to explain a bit of how to use these new stuff. Hope you like it.

[previewyoutube=hSLtSgIeWbQ;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]
Here is the full changelog list:[/b]

[list]
[*]  Now when Ctrl+B assigns selected points to selected bone, it removes selected points that already belongs to other bones. This helps to keep every point with one just single bone parent.

[*]  Now is possible interpolate points that belongs to some bone, even if the bone is not seleceted. This helps to create more animation detais even you if dont have the originals keyframes used to animate the bones.

[*]  Bone interpolation bug fixes.

[*]  Now, a double click with "alt" holding down, selects the whole object and let it in the spotlight mode.

[*]  Now when ESC is pressed over render area, all selection is cleared.

[*]  Now when ESC is pressed over timeline, all timeline selection is cleared.

[*]  Now there is a new feature that makes selected brushes points, follow the animation steps of their parent shape/object. This helps to give more detail to a animation even that it's finished.

[*]  Now when you select a group in the group name area, if you hold Ctrl, you keep all selection intact and adds all this selected group points to selection. 

[*]  Now there is a new feature that "Freezes" texture count used to render brushes. This is usefull to keep the brush aspect during animation.

[*]  Now you can use merge feature to merge a content from shape library to your current scene evan if you have more than one skeleton/bones with same names of the shape library content. For this, just select the skeleton you one merge before do the merge.

[*]  Opening old projects versions in .json format bug fix.
[/list]

notes.title: Arttista 1.8 is out!
notes.content:
[b]Arttista 1.8 [/b]version is here with a new very useful feature that allows you import content from your shape library and merge with your current scene respecting your current bones positions and poses. This means that you can draw your character at different angles and then, when you import it to your scene, you select wich frame you want import to and your character shapes will be at same pose your bones already are. This is awesome, cause after draw your character from different angles, you dont have to draw it anymore and just reuse it every time the view and pose you want it to. Check it in next video:

[b]How you can reuse different views of same character in animation[/b]
[previewyoutube=LM92QHBoV14;full][/previewyoutube]
[b]Besides that, there is new features and also bug fixes too.[/b]
[list]
[*]Now you can import just a single frame from shape library and this new content will be merged with current content respecting bones position if new bones have same nomes of current scene bones

[*]Now you can unjoin brushes from some shape using SHIFT + J

[*]Now you can assign selected points to selected bone just pressing CTRL + B

[*]And you can deassign selected points from selected bone just pressing SHIFT + B

[*]Now is possible to remove Items from Shape Library

[*]Now you can do a zoom in or zoom out just holdind the ALT on keyboard and keeping mouse middle button down.

[*]Better CTRL + Z algorithm for free hand objects

[*]Now brushes objects can also be filled too (CTRL + T)

[*]Now brushes objects can be closed form too (CTRL + E)

[*]Bugfix while exporting to shape library

[*]General use bugs fixes



[/list]

notes.title: A new "Game Sprite Sheet" animation exporter in Arttista 1.5.5
notes.content:
[b]Arttista 1.5.5[/b] is out now with it's new game sprite sheet animation exporter. Now you can easily create animations specially designed for 2D Games that uses Sprite Sheet concept. Just check it out in this video where i show how it works. I also show a little bit of Arttista animation system and how you can use it to make character animations using a simple example.

[previewyoutube=Q0T382q-0vU;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]So, whats new on Arttista 1.5.5?[/b]

[list]
[*]Implementation of Game Sprite Sheet Exporter.

[*]Now, it's possible to do a vertical or horizontal flip in a range of frames, selected in timeline,
instead only in the current frame. That means you can invert a range of animation.

[*]Now, it's possible to resize your drawing or animation to any resolution you wanna to, with all objects
resized too.

[*]Now, there is a panning tool instead mouse scroll pressing only.

[*]Now, there is a zooming tool instead mouse scrolling only.

[*]Fix bug dureing importing .art files with animations

[*]Now, when you draw using lines(when you hold CTRL), you dont neet to worry about control points 
when edit these lines after. Lines will always be lines now.

[*]On MacOS, there is a bug fix for when you tell MacOS to load you .art files with Arttista. Now, 
Arttista do it correctly.

[*]Now, the size/width of vertices/points, are also, different for each frame, so this way you can have
differente sizes of foreground during animation. This is helpfull when you want to make something get
bigger or smaller, and wants the foreground changes too.

[/list]



I hope you enjoy it.
Helmuth Schmitz
